fact.text: 85 years ago this week, in a single day, 9,200 residents of the Kaunas ghetto were shot at the city's Ninth Fort; about half of them were children.

heads_up: Lapkričio 1–2 d. – ilgasis Visų šventųjų ir Vėlinių savaitgalis; policija perspėja apie sustiprintą kontrolę keliuose.

lithuania.headline: Koalicija sutarė didinti mokesčius, biudžetas strigo komitetuose
lithuania.summary: Premjeras Mindaugas Sinkevičius paskelbė, kad koalicija sutarė dėl mokesčių didinimo, tačiau 2027 m. biudžeto projektas, numatantis 3,8 proc. BVP deficitą ir 48,2 proc. BVP skolą, stringa Seimo komitetuose. Koalicijos partneriai demokratai sako, kad kol kas už jį nebalsuos, kol Finansų ministerija nepateiks deficito mažinimo plano.
lithuania.context: Finansų ministras Taurimas Valys šį rudenį Seimui pateikė 2027 m. biudžetą su 3,8 proc. BVP deficitu. Prezidentas Gitanas Nausėda kritikavo Vyriausybę, kad ši nepateikė plano, kaip mažinti deficitą, ir tikisi, kad jis neviršys 3 proc. BVP. Nuo to laiko koalicijos partneriai ir Seimo komitetai kelia savo sąlygas.

lithuania.headline: Valstybės gynimo taryba svarsto oro gynybą ir visuotinį šaukimą
lithuania.summary: Prezidentas Gitanas Nausėda ketvirtadienį šaukia Valstybės gynimo tarybos posėdį, kuriame bus aptarta integruota oro erdvės gynyba, įspėjimo apie oro atakas sistemos pakeitimai po šį mėnesį nukritusio drono ir perėjimas prie visuotinio šaukimo. Krašto apsaugos ministras Robertas Kaunas sako, kad visuotinis šaukimas nuo 2030 m. įmanomas, bet turi rizikų.
lithuania.context: Lietuva šauktinių kariuomenę atkūrė 2015 m., po Rusijos įvykdytos Krymo aneksijos; šiemet planuota pašaukti 5 tūkst. jaunuolių. Rugsėjį prezidento vadovaujama taryba pranešė siūlysianti paspartinti visuotinio šaukimo įvedimą, o šią savaitę konservatorių lyderis Laurynas Kasčiūnas pasiūlė jį įvesti 2030 m. Kitų metų biudžete gynybai numatyta 5 proc. BVP, arba 4,8 mlrd. eurų.

lithuania.headline: Vytautas Landsbergis paguldytas į Santaros klinikas
lithuania.summary: 94-erių Vytautas Landsbergis antradienį atvežtas į Santaros klinikas, LRT duomenimis – į intensyviosios terapijos skyrių. Sūnaus teigimu, būklė stabili ir gerėja, o sveikatos pablogėjimas greičiausiai susijęs su infekcija.
lithuania.context: Landsbergis 1990 m. vadovavo Aukščiausiajai Tarybai, paskelbusiai Lietuvos nepriklausomybės atkūrimą; balandį jam buvo atliktos dvi akių operacijos.

world.headline: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 in Spain
world.summary: A Renfe train carrying 397 passengers ploughed into the back of a stationary Iryo train with 147 on board near Urda, south of Madrid, killing at least 68 and sending 107 to hospital. The transport minister said a control centre made an 'inexplicable' decision to let the trains move again without speed limits after a computer failure; Spain began three days of mourning.
world.why: Covered by 8 outlets, top of front pages
world.context: It is Spain's second deadly high-speed crash this year: in January, 46 people died when Renfe and Iryo trains collided on the same line near Adamuz.

world.headline: UK budget gives households £100 energy payment
world.summary: Chancellor John Healey's first budget gives 20 million households a one-off £100 energy payment in January, offers low-carbon upgrade loans of up to £35,000 and promises to end gas standing charges, as energy prices rise over the Middle East war. The fiscal watchdog cut next year's growth forecast to 1% and raised its inflation forecast to 3.4%.
world.why: Covered by 6 outlets, BBC front page
world.context: It is the first budget since Andy Burnham became prime minister, with household energy bills at their highest in three years.

world.headline: EU backs away from 'associate member' offer to Canada
world.summary: As an EU-Canada summit opened in Montreal, the EU dropped its offer to start 'associate membership' talks with Canada after objections from member states; the draft statement instead promises to define 'an ever closer association, short of full membership' by 2027.
world.context: Canada has sought closer ties with Europe since Donald Trump's tariffs and annexation talk strained relations, and in January PM Mark Carney urged 'middle powers' to work together. Last month Commission president Ursula von der Leyen surprised EU capitals by floating associate membership, prompting political and legal pushback.

world.headline: Hackers leak data on 41,000 US Homeland Security staff
world.summary: A hacker group called the Department of Peace took names, job titles, work phones, emails and office locations of more than 41,000 DHS staff, including 21,000 border agents and about 6,600 ICE agents, via the department's Okta login system; it was published online by DDoSecrets.
world.context: It is the third leak or hack of a US government agency in recent weeks, after breaches of FBI and Pentagon personnel data.

interesting.headline: Apple launches touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro
interesting.summary: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro has an OLED display and M5 Pro or Max chips and starts at $2,899 (14-inch) and $3,399 (16-inch); fully specced with 16TB of storage it costs $14,549. Preorders open on 30 October.
interesting.why: Covered by 5 outlets, top of tech news
interesting.context: Steve Jobs once called a touchscreen Mac 'ergonomically terrible'.

interesting.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon model
interesting.summary: Google says Gemini 4 Carbon tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, with big gains in finding and fixing security bugs. For now it is only available to selected cybersecurity defence companies.
interesting.context: It comes just two weeks after Google released Gemini 4 Argon.

interesting.headline: Brewers win first World Series in franchise history
interesting.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to take the series; catcher William Contreras was named MVP after hitting .381.
interesting.why: Covered by 5 outlets, top of sports news

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: Russia said 613 Ukrainian drones flew towards Moscow overnight, 231 of them shot down near the city, and restricted flights at Vnukovo and Domodedovo airports; Russia hit Kharkiv, damaging an educational building.
ongoing.context: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, after annexing Crimea in 2014. Kyiv pushed Russian forces back from the capital and later in the north-east and Kherson, but the front has since largely stalled. This month a US-brokered truce began in occupied Oleshky and was widened across the Kherson region, ahead of planned US-Russia-Ukraine talks.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Iran said it is discussing with mediators how to implement its seven-day plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while rejecting 'unacceptable' ideas in a new Qatari draft; Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth fired the Pentagon's top military planner as Trump weighs new strikes.
ongoing.context: Tensions date back to the 1979 Islamic Revolution and grew over Iran's nuclear programme. In February the US and Israel went to war with Iran, which took control of the Strait of Hormuz, prompting a US naval blockade of Iranian ports. A June deal on a path to settlement collapsed, and Qatar is now mediating ahead of the US midterms on 3 November.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: The Houthis struck Aden airport in Yemen after issuing an evacuation warning.
ongoing.context: Yemen's Houthi rebels seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 to back the government. A truce from 2022 largely held, but fighting with Saudi Arabia reignited during the regional war with Iran, with Houthi missile strikes on Riyadh and Saudi oil sites.

ongoing.title: Protests across France and Europe
ongoing.update: UN experts condemned 'excessive use of force' against French student protests, where several thousand people, mostly minors, have been arrested; Albania introduced fines of up to €5,500, six times the average monthly salary, for anyone present at a protest that turns violent.
ongoing.context: French students began protesting in mid-September over run-down schools and later the cost of living, and youth-led protests have since spread across Europe, including months of anti-government rallies in Albania. Under-35s hold just 2.8% of European household wealth.
